# Data
Load libraries
```{r}
pacman::p_load(sf, # spatial
               here, 
               tidyverse, 
               rio, # for importing
               table1, # make table1
               lubridate,
               ncf, #correlation
               xtable, # export table1
               fuzzyjoin # joining with some inexact
               )
```

Read in shapefiles
```{r}
## Read in case shapefile - TIRS_SINAVE_22_23
sus <- st_read(dsn = here("data"), 
                 layer = "TIRS_SINAVE_22_23")
## Cluster shapefile
clusters <- st_read(dsn = here("data"),
                    layer = "Cluster final 2021 actualizado")
```

SINAVE raw data
```{r}
season21 <- here::here("data", "SINAVE_Data", 
                       "datos_abiertos_dengue_301221.csv") %>%
  rio::import() %>% 
  dplyr::as_tibble()

season22 <- here::here("data", "SINAVE_Data", 
                       "datos_abiertos_dengue_011222.csv") %>%
  rio::import() %>% 
  dplyr::as_tibble()

season23 <- here::here("data", "SINAVE_Data", 
                       "datos_abiertos_dengue_061223.csv") %>%
  rio::import() %>% 
  dplyr::as_tibble()
```


## Questions
```{r}
# are there suspected cases for both sources for both years?
table(sus$Source, sus$Year)

# diagnosis labels for each source
sinave <- sus %>% filter(Source=="SINAVE")
tirs <- sus %>% filter(Source=="TIRS")
unique(sinave$Diagnosis)
unique(tirs$Diagnosis)

# only dengue?
tirs_DENV <- tirs %>% filter(str_detect(Diagnosis, "DENV")) # 245 cases
table(tirs_DENV$Year, tirs_DENV$Diagnosis)
# what DENV diagnosis, for which years?
```
Ok now I have a dataset that has all the TIRS cases labeled by infection type 
WHICH WAS HARDER THAN I THOUGHT IT'D BE
```{r}
# all dengue cases from the TIRS trial
tirs_all_cases <- readRDS("all_cases_labeled.rds")
tirs_all_denv <- tirs_all_cases %>% 
  filter(denv_case == 1 | denv_zikv == 1 | denv_chikv == 1) # 327 (includes DENV coinfections)

# all dengue cases given to me in the one file
tirs_DENV # 245 

#ok? are these all ? mostly? the same people?
## i'll rbind select variables of each...
sub_trial_data <- tirs_all_denv %>% # 327 cases
  select(PPID, evnt_year, var6_symp_date, arm) %>% 
  rename(id = PPID,
         event_year = evnt_year,
         symp_onset = var6_symp_date,
         trial_arm = arm) %>% 
  mutate(source = "Trial Data")
sub_govt_data <- tirs_DENV %>% # 245 cases
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  select(ID, Year, Onset_symp, Arm_1TIRS) %>% 
  rename(id = ID,
         event_year = Year,
         symp_onset = Onset_symp,
         trial_arm = Arm_1TIRS) %>% 
  mutate(source = "MoH Data")
test_tirs_cases <- rbind(sub_trial_data, sub_govt_data)

# ok how can i make sure to only grab the non-duplicates?
tirs_all_denv %>% count(PPID) %>% #number of times an indv was infected w dengue
  count(n) # there are four IDs that have two events, two that have three

# which ones have multiple events
sub_govt_data %>% count(id) %>% filter(n > 1) # not just first events
tirs_all_denv %>% count(PPID) %>% 
  filter(n > 1)

# what about by year? # this works, all one year so group by that
tirs_all_denv %>% count(PPID, evnt_year) %>% #number of times an indv was infected w dengue
  count(n) 

test_tirs_cases %>% arrange(id, event_year) #some duplicates...
only_in_one <- anti_join(sub_trial_data, sub_govt_data, 
                         by = c("id", "event_year"))
# ok so all moh cases are included in the TIRS cases (so they're not extra ones
# picked up by the MoH that weren't picked up by the clinical trial)
# all extra cases are ones picked up by the trial
# 82 extra cases

tirs_all_denv %>% filter(PPID %in% only_in_one$id)
# uhhh all these are different trial arms, different block types (central vs.
# periphery)
```

```{r}

# all moh data including block_id from gonzalo
sub_sinave_block <- sinave_block %>%

         event_year = evnt_year,

#ok...do any of the sinave and tirs match by symptom onset date? age? cluster? block?
young_sinave %>% arrange(cluster_id, block_id, event_year)
young_trial %>% arrange(cluster_id, block_id, event_year)

# if trial arm, event year, cluster_id match exactly
# if age, block_id off by +-1?
fuzzy_inner_join(young_sinave, young_trial,
                 by = c("trial_arm", "event_year", "cluster_id", "age", 
                        "block_id"),
                 match_fun = list(`==`, `==`, `==`, 
                                  function(x, y) abs(x - y) <= 1,
                                  function(x, y) abs(x - y) <= 2)) %>% 
  relocate(c(id.x, id.y, symp_onset.x, symp_onset.y,
             cluster_id.x, cluster_id.y, block_id.x, block_id.y, age.x, age.y, 
             event_year.x, event_year.y, trial_arm.x, trial_arm.y), 
           .before = id.x)

# 551712A 2023, 551725A 2023, 551918A 2023, 551921B 2023, 551921C 2023,

# okay i'm just going to assume these are basically the same people...maybe some

# 311412A 2023, 251424A 2023
```

## Some Cleaning
Only actual cases
```{r}
cases <- sus %>% 
  filter(Diagnosis != "Negativo") %>% 
  filter(Comentario != "Negativo" | is.na(Comentario))

unique(cases$Diagnosis) # only actual diagnoses
#unique(cases$Comentario) # there was one that had Negativo as a comment rather than under diagnosis

cases$ABD_type <- sub('.*\\+ ', '', cases$Diagnosis)
cases$ABD_type <- sub(' *.', '', cases$ABD_type)
```

SINAVE Data
```{r}
s21 <- season21 %>% 
  # only want data for Merida (050 MUNICIPO_RES and 31 ENTIDAD_RES)
  filter(MUNICIPIO_RES == 50 & ENTIDAD_RES == 31) %>% 
  # change symptom onset date to match cases dataset (i.e., weeks since 
  #  start of ABD season)
  mutate(Week_onset = ymd(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS),
         Week_onset = epiweek(Week_onset), #epiweek????
         Year = year(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS)) %>% 
  relocate(c(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS, Week_onset), .before = ID_REGISTRO)

s22 <- season22 %>% 
  # only want data for Merida (050 MUNICIPO_RES and 31 ENTIDAD_RES)
  filter(MUNICIPIO_RES == 50 & ENTIDAD_RES == 31) %>% 
  # change symptom onset date to match cases dataset (i.e., weeks since 
  #  start of ABD season)
  mutate(Week_onset = ymd(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS),
         Week_onset = epiweek(Week_onset), #epiweek????
         Year = year(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS)) %>%
  relocate(c(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS, Week_onset), .before = ID_REGISTRO)

s23 <- season23 %>% 
  # only want data for Merida (050 MUNICIPO_RES and 31 ENTIDAD_RES)
  filter(MUNICIPIO_RES == 50 & ENTIDAD_RES == 31) %>% 
  # change symptom onset date to match cases dataset (i.e., weeks since 
  #  start of ABD season)
  mutate(Week_onset = ymd(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS),
         Week_onset = epiweek(Week_onset), #epiweek????
         Year = year(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS)) %>%
  relocate(c(FECHA_SIGN_SINTOMAS, Week_onset), .before = ID_REGISTRO)
```

# Map
By source
```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_sf(data = clusters, linewidth = 0.05, aes(fill = as.factor(TIRS)),
          alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_sf(data = cases, size = 0.75, stroke = 0,
          aes(color = as.factor(Source))) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("ivory4", "dodgerblue4"), 
                    name = "TIRS", labels = c("No", "Yes")) + 
  guides(color = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("cadetblue3", "coral2"), 
                    name = "Source", labels = c("TIRS", "SINAVE")) +
  theme_minimal()
ggsave("cases_source.pdf")
```

# Table 1
Formatting
```{r}
cases$Arm_1TIRS <- 
  factor(cases$Arm_1TIRS, levels = c(0, 1),
         labels = c("Control",
                    "TIRS Intervention"))
cases$Year <- factor(cases$Year)
cases$Age <- as.numeric(cases$Age)

label(cases$Age) <- "Age"
label(cases$Arm_1TIRS) <- "Trial Arm"
label(cases$Year) <- "Year*"
label(cases$Week_onset) <- "Week of Symptom Onset <sup>†</sup>"

footnote <- "*In 2023, there was a large outbreak of DENV-3 <br> <sup>†</sup> Week of the year"
```

Make Table
```{r}
case_tab <- table1(~ Age + Year + Arm_1TIRS + Week_onset | Source, data = cases,
       footnote=footnote)
case_tab <- as.data.frame(case_tab)
print(xtable(case_tab, type = "latex"), file = "case_tab.tex")
```

# Case Data over Time
Combine all SINAVE data? all data in general? 
```{r}
sinave <- do.call("rbind", list(s21, s22, s23))

table(sinave$ESTATUS_CASO) # 1 likely; 2 confirmed; 3 discarded

# we want only confirmed cases? (ESTATUS_CASO == 2)
sinave_cases <- sinave %>% 
  filter(ESTATUS_CASO == 2)
```

and get case counts
```{r}
sinave_case_num <- sinave_cases %>% 
  count(Year, Week_onset) %>% 
  mutate(Year = as.character(Year))
trial_case_num <- cases %>% 
  count(Year, Week_onset) %>% 
  st_drop_geometry() %>% 
  mutate(Year = as.character(Year)) %>% 
  add_row(Year = "2021", Week_onset = 1, n = 0)
```

With same y axis
```{r}
ggplot() +
  geom_col(data = sinave_case_num,
           aes(x = Week_onset, y = n, fill = "SINAVE"),
           alpha = 0.6) + 
  geom_col(data = trial_case_num,
           aes(x = Week_onset, y = n, fill = "TIRS")) +
  facet_wrap(~ Year, ncol = 1) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TIRS" = "steelblue",
                               "SINAVE" = "firebrick")) +
  labs(x = "Week of Symptom Onset",
       y = "Number of Cases",
       fill = "Source",
       title = "ABD Cases by Week (TIRS vs. SINAVE)") +
  scale_x_continuous(
    breaks = seq(1, 53, by = 2)
  ) +
  theme_classic()
ggsave("cases_by_week.pdf")
```
